_comment: The reviewed inventory of every cost input in the public API's @time annotations (M2-04). tools/evidence/check_bounds.py checks that every public function whose @time is not O(1) maps to entries here and renders resource-bounds.md from this file. Enforcement: 'configuration' (a Kconfig limit), 'admission' (the kernel refuses beyond it), 'structural' (follows from another bound) or 'application' (the kernel does not limit it; the application must). 'masked' says whether the cost runs with interrupts masked.

bounds.input: threads waiting on one wait queue
bounds.bound: at most the live threads: a thread waits on at most one queue
bounds.limit: base: 254 thread IDs; tiny: CONFIG_EMB_PRIORITY_COUNT - 1 threads
bounds.profiles: base: PRIORITY_FIFO insert walks from the tail, O(waiters), FIFO O(1); tiny: bitmap set O(1), first waiter O(1) or the raised-thread scan
bounds.evidence: SPEC-004 §11; the reference model's queue-order invariant

bounds.bound: at most one per thread, so at most the live threads
bounds.profiles: base: doubly linked list, insert O(armed) from the tail, removal O(1); tiny: singly linked list, insert and removal O(armed)
bounds.evidence: SPEC-003 §5.1, SPEC-012 §13; the model's one-timeout-per-thread invariant

bounds.bound: not limited by the kernel: at most the mutex objects the application creates
bounds.profiles: the same singly linked owned list on every profile; acquisition appends, release and recomputation walk it

bounds.bound: CONFIG_EMB_PI_MAX_DEPTH hops; each hop recomputes O(owned) and requeues O(waiters)
bounds.profiles: checked builds fault at the limit, release builds stop propagating (no complete inheritance beyond it); deadlock detection inspects the same number of links

bounds.bound: CONFIG_EMB_PRIORITY_COUNT - 1 slots, only while some thread runs above its base priority
bounds.limit: CONFIG_EMB_PRIORITY_COUNT, at most the architecture word width
bounds.profiles: tiny only; base selects through the per-priority bitmap

bounds.bound: O(1) on base (bitmap and per-priority lists); the table scan on tiny
bounds.profiles: one decision per preemption point; batch wakes reschedule once

bounds.input: waiters woken at once (destroy with EMB_OBJ_ABORT_WAITERS)
bounds.bound: the waiters of the destroyed object
bounds.profiles: one section, one reschedule at the end

bounds.input: diagnostic identity scan at thread init
bounds.bound: 254 IDs on list profiles, CONFIG_EMB_PRIORITY_COUNT - 1 on tiny
bounds.limit: fixed per profile; EMB_ENOMEM beyond it
bounds.profiles: bitmap scan from the lowest ID

bounds.bound: at most 254 (the ID space)
bounds.profiles: base only (no list on tiny); walked by thread init and emb_thread_foreach

bounds.input: active objects of one type (semaphores, mutexes, event flags, condition variables, message queues, work queues, timers)
bounds.bound: not limited by the kernel: the objects the application initializes
bounds.profiles: with CONFIG_EMB_OBJ_LIST only (not on tiny); walked by init

bounds.input: bytes copied for one message queue operation
bounds.bound: at most two items (a receive that refills from a waiting sender), each item_size bytes
bounds.limit: CONFIG_EMB_MSGQ_MAX_ITEM (default 64, tiny 16); init refuses a larger item_size
bounds.profiles: a byte loop under the object lock on every profile

bounds.bound: not limited by the kernel: the timers the application starts
bounds.profiles: list scheduler only; insertion walks from the tail of the timer list (ADR-047), removal O(1); an expiry pass handles each due timer once

bounds.bound: the stack size the application supplied
bounds.profiles: the high-water scan exists only with CONFIG_EMB_STACK_STATS; init fills the stack in checked and statistics builds

bounds.bound: the EMB_*_DEFINE objects linked into the image
bounds.profiles: prekernel only

bounds.input: application callbacks the kernel calls (fault hook, trace sink, foreach visitor)
bounds.bound: not bounded by the kernel
bounds.profiles: the fault hook and the trace sink can run with interrupts masked; the foreach visitor runs under the scheduler lock

bounds.input: the port's fault action (halt or reset)
bounds.bound: does not return
bounds.profiles: CONFIG_EMB_FAULT_ACTION

bounds.bound: at most 255: emb_device_t.dep_count is 8 bits, and the generator emits them from the description
bounds.profiles: base with CONFIG_EMB_DEVICE (off on tiny and AVR)

bounds.bound: the count passed; the board's table holds at most 65,535 (a 16-bit count)
bounds.limit: configuration: the board's devices, fixed at generation
bounds.profiles: base with CONFIG_EMB_DEVICE

bounds.bound: not limited by the kernel: the requests callers have submitted and not yet seen complete
bounds.profiles: a singly linked FIFO per device; cancel walks it in the device's critical section

bounds.input: a driver's operations (init, start, stop, suspend, resume) and a request's completion target
bounds.bound: not bounded by the kernel: each driver's own, stated with its class
bounds.profiles: called outside the device's critical section; completion delivery too

bounds.input: bytes of one UART request, or of a polled call
bounds.bound: the caller's: the length it passes; a read also stops at the ring's bytes when it starts
bounds.profiles: base with CONFIG_EMB_DRV_UART; the ring is drained into a starting read in the device's critical section

bounds.bound: the caller's: the length it passes; the controller is serviced at most a FIFO's frames per interrupt
bounds.profiles: base with CONFIG_EMB_DRV_SPI; frames move in the driver's interrupt, outside the device's critical section

bounds.input: bytes and segments of one I2C transaction or listen
bounds.bound: the caller's: the segments and lengths it passes, each segment checked once at submit; a listen stops storing at its buffer's size
bounds.profiles: base with CONFIG_EMB_DRV_I2C; bytes move in the driver's interrupts, one byte or a FIFO's worth at a time
